scope: Prepared nine-page responses served only in an isolated browser, using current live assets; not a production deployment.

checks.action: Calculate each type of drink you actually had, then add the results for the whole week. Compare that weekly total with the UK low-risk guideline of no more than 14 units regularly; this is not a safe allowance for one session.

Write down the date, height, weight and BMI. If your BMI is below 35, add a waist-to-height measurement for a second perspective. Take an unexpected result or questions about your health to a qualified professional.

Save the maintenance estimate and check that the activity choice matches a normal week. Use it as a planning estimate, then review your real weight trend and how the plan feels over 2–4 weeks. Do not automatically subtract a large deficit or eat back walking calories.

Record the range as context, then compare it with your current weight, waist and health history. The bottom of the range is not a goal. If you want to set a weight target, use an individual discussion rather than selecting a number from this range alone.

Check the selected planning level first. Once you have an appropriate target, look at protein in the meals you already eat and spread it across those meals. Kidney disease or another condition needing individual nutrition advice takes priority over this estimate.

Measure halfway between the bottom of your ribs and the top of your hips, after breathing out naturally. Record waist, height and date so the next measurement is comparable. Use the ratio as a discussion point alongside BMI and other health information.

Use time and consistency as the main targets. Choose a repeatable walk that fits your current ability, record the minutes and repeat it through the week. The calorie estimate is for comparison; it is not a food allowance or a reason to push through symptoms.

Start with regular drinks through the day, including meals. The NHS uses 6–8 cups or glasses of fluid as a general guide; tea, coffee and other suitable drinks count too. Needs change with heat and activity. Follow any clinician-set fluid restriction instead of this calculator.
